title: Tuples with Bounded Differences
statement:
You are given three arrays `A`, `B` and `C`, each sorted in non-decreasing order, and a non-negative integer `d`.

A tuple `(i, j, k)` is **valid** if the three chosen values `A[i]`, `B[j]` and `C[k]` have all pairwise differences at most `d`:

`|A[i] - B[j]| ≤ d`, `|A[i] - C[k]| ≤ d` and `|B[j] - C[k]| ≤ d`.

Equivalently, the largest of the three values minus the smallest is at most `d`. Tuples are distinguished by their indices, so equal values at different positions count as different tuples.

The number of valid tuples can be huge, so instead of listing them, print how many there are.

**Follow-up:** The interviewer first asked for the straightforward `O(|A| · |B| · |C|)` solution and then pushed for faster ones: a two-pointer approach and finally a binary-search based approach. Be ready to discuss how each improves on the previous one.
inputFormat:
The first line contains four integers `p`, `q`, `r` and `d`: the sizes of `A`, `B`, `C` and the bound.
The next three lines contain the arrays `A` (`p` integers), `B` (`q` integers) and `C` (`r` integers).
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the number of valid tuples.
constraints: each array is sorted in non-decreasing order

examples.explanation: With d = 2 the valid value triples (A, B, C) are (1, 2, 3), (4, 2, 3), (4, 5, 3), (4, 5, 6) and (8, 9, 10). For example (4, 2, 6) is not valid because 6 - 2 = 4 > 2.
With d = 0 all three values must be equal. Every one of the 2 · 2 · 2 index combinations has all values equal to 5.
The only element of B is 20, which is more than 1 away from every element of A and of C, so no triple fits.

hints: Checking every triple costs O(p · q · r). Is there a way to avoid looking at triples you know are invalid?
Look at a tuple through its smallest value x. Then both other values must lie in the window [x, x + d].

Fix the smallest element and count how many elements of each of the other two arrays fall in the window with binary search; multiply the counts. Break ties between equal minimums by array order so every tuple is counted exactly once.
